verdict_text: NO. The plan adds the scaled task vector 1 into the base MLP tensors (the first `add_`) before it computes task vector 2, so the second `subtract_` takes ft2 against the already-modified base rather than the unmodified base. The result is out = base + 0.24·(ft1−base) + 0.4·(ft2−base) instead of the formula in Required result step 2, which is exactly the ordering hazard the Objective section warns about. This will fail the 1e-5 relative-error check on the 48 merged tensors. Additionally, step 1 only asserts ft1 and ft2 each have 160 tensors and that non-MLP base tensors equal their ft counterparts; it never checks that base has 160 names or that ft1/ft2 contain no names absent from base, so "same tensor names" is only partially verified.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
